scope: Follow-up to canvas-memory-audit-20261022.json. Direct upload preparation only; resident dense texture budget is unchanged. No physical pen latency claim.

packing.scope: Five alternating-order pairs of 100 preparations per case, release CPU only. Shared composite, source document, upload queue and GPU allocation excluded. Exact image sizes/pixels checked outside timing. Old and new paths in the same test binary.

display_comparison.scope: Supported 512/2048-square documents: one dense flat base plus sparse additional layers, 1/8/32 layers; eager padded display shared with navigator. Synchronous comparator and production background tile compositor using existing parallel pixel bands; sliced cursor is failure fallback. Owner 2 ms allowance checked between controls/publications, which can overrun. One sequential drain per case; 1 ms polling sleeps when awaiting worker, no UI frame waits. Owner update timings exclude worker execution; completed-worker milliseconds sum kernel elapsed wall time, not all-core CPU time. Drain wall includes polling and image reconstruction, excludes final pixel oracle. Every padded pixel and emitted-payload accounting checked outside call timing. Texture bytes are RGBA payload with theoretical complete mip chain, not measured GPU allocation. Metadata/prefix bytes count owned vector capacities, excluding weak allocation headers/allocator overhead. Preparation peak estimates worker output capacity plus imaging buffers and per-frame pending canvas image payload, excludes frozen source snapshots, resident cache/history/document and validation copies. This is not RSS, a total memory budget or dense 32-layer certification.
display_comparison.method: Three alternating frozen build runs per version, 48 cases each, no competing compiler jobs. Two repeat pairs investigate variable whole-display results; all runs retained. Whole owner timings are comparable; conversion now falls under synchronous composite_ms and async upload_ms, so isolated phase timers are not directly comparable to earlier reports. Pixel and coherent publication oracles passed.

validation.native_captures: OpenGL and DirectX 12 each pixel-identical to the preceding build on the same renderer
